source.repro: Invert the hosted hs1ToMm39.over.chain.pif.gz (HOSTING.md) back to PAF from its t rows: gzip -dc hosted.pif.gz | awk -F'\t' 'BEGIN{OFS="\t"} $1 ~ /^t/ { $1=substr($1,2); q=$6; ql=$7; qs=$8; qe=$9; $6=$1; $7=$2; $8=$3; $9=$4; $1=q; $2=ql; $3=qs; $4=qe; print }' > hosted.paf. Rebuild with the current writer: jbrowse make-pif hosted.paf --out new.pif.gz (default --coarse 10000). Per tier: gzip -dc <pif> | awk -F'\t' '{ c=substr($1,1,1); n[c]++; b[c]+=length($0)+1 } END { for (k in n) print k, n[k], b[k] }'; the gzip column is one perspective's T rows piped through gzip -c | wc -c; the fold census runs coarsenCigar(cg, 10000) over every PAF row and counts gapCount/opCount and the ops' lengths.
source.notes: Disk cost of the coarse CIGAR (ADR-104) against the split format it replaced, on the one eukaryote-scale PIF that is hosted. Both arms are the same 75,076 alignments; the old tier has 662 more rows because it split at indels >= 10 kb, the new one is one row per alignment. Bytes are uncompressed per perspective (the T rows; Q is identical in size), so a whole-genome pass reads one of them. Every one of the 75,076 folds closed on its columns, so the columns-verbatim fallback never fired on chain2paf output. 5,047 rows (6.7%) carry a fold; 1,678 of those have no kept indel and exist only because a lopsided cluster of small indels bent the path. 142,236 indels are kept, 96,538 of them between 5 and 10 kb (kept by the half-gap rule, sub-pixel at the 10,000 bp/px threshold): they are about two thirds of the fold's bytes and are the price of the interpolation bound. The largest fold is one 90 Mb chr4 chain, 9,038 ops, 72 kB; the longest run is 80.6 Mb, so nothing chunks at 2^28.
